scenes.title: SMOOTH DOES NOT MEAN CLEAN
scenes.overlay: Check the data behind the chart.
scenes.narration: A chart can look smooth and still be misleading. Before trusting a signal, ask what feed produced it, when each bar belongs, and whether the history is complete.

scenes.title: NAME THE FEED
scenes.overlay: IEX and SIP are not the same.
scenes.narration: Feed choice changes coverage. Alpaca's market data documentation distinguishes IEX, a single exchange, from SIP, which consolidates activity across US exchanges. A chart built from one feed is not automatically comparable with a chart built from another. Record the feed, not just the symbol.

scenes.title: READ THE BAR TIME
scenes.narration: A bar timestamp labels its aggregation interval. Alpaca explains that a one-minute bar is timestamped at the start of the minute, not at the time you happen to view it. Check the interval, timezone, session and latest update before calling data current.

scenes.title: CHECK EVERY PAGE
scenes.overlay: A short response may be incomplete.
scenes.narration: A missing candle is not a zero-price candle. Historical-bars responses can contain fewer points than the requested limit, and the API provides a next-page token when more data is available. Check pagination and gaps before calculating indicators or assuming the series is complete.

scenes.title: KEEP ADJUSTMENTS CONSISTENT
scenes.narration: Corporate-action settings matter too. The historical-bars endpoint supports raw, split, dividend and all adjustment modes. Keep the chosen adjustment consistent across the test and document it. If the feed, session or adjustment is unclear, pause the paper test instead of guessing.

scenes.title: VERIFY BEFORE YOU TEST
scenes.narration: Build a small data checklist: source, timestamp, session, pagination, adjustment and missing values. Then test the same rules in a paper simulation, record the limitations, and accept NO TRADE when the inputs fail. claims.claim: Alpaca describes IEX as a single exchange and SIP as consolidated activity from all US exchanges.
Alpaca's market-data FAQ describes a minute bar timestamp as the left side, or start, of the aggregation interval.
The historical-bars API may return fewer data points than requested and exposes next_page_token when more pages are available.
The historical-bars API offers raw, split, dividend and all adjustment modes.
